title: A delete, a missed repair, and a row that comes back
captions: Three replicas hold row 7. You delete it at QUORUM. A and B write a tombstone with a newer timestamp. C is down and misses the delete. It stays down for days, past the 3-hour hint window.
Reads still work. A QUORUM read merges the answers and keeps the newest one. The tombstone (t=2) beats the row (t=1), so the row stays deleted.
The default gc_grace_seconds is 10 days. After it, compaction on A and B may drop the tombstone and the old row. C still has row 7, with no tombstone.
Now repair compares the replicas. Nothing says row 7 was deleted. C's copy looks like live data, so it is copied back to A and B.
The fix: repair every node before gc_grace_seconds runs out. C then receives the tombstone while A and B still have it.
